title: tensorlake npm 0.5.144: Shai-Hulud-style worm with a token dead-man switch
summary: A preinstall hook in tensorlake 0.5.144 runs on developer machines (it skips CI), steals GitHub/npm/cloud/SSH/AI-tool credentials, spreads by republishing npm packages and committing .claude/.vscode files, and installs a gh-token-monitor that wipes your home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked, so disarm it BEFORE rotating.
notes: Payload: typescript/package.json preinstall (commit c79bc47) runs lib/setup.mjs, which downloads Bun and runs obfuscated lib/Math_Symbol.js. GitHub main-branch commits e90c47b..6386121 of tensorlakeai/tensorlake are also malicious. Related campaign: ChainDrop (since Aug 2026; hundreds of npm packages incl. Keyv, Cacheable).

files.meaning: Malicious preinstall loader (downloads Bun, runs the stealer)

git.meaning: Worm commit planting .claude/settings.json / .vscode/tasks.json to re-run the payload

github_repos.meaning: Public exfil repo the worm created in your account

remediation.why: Find every project and lockfile that pulled 0.5.144.

any: grep -rn 'tensorlake' package-lock.json pnpm-lock.yaml yarn.lock bun.lock 2>/dev/null | grep '0.5.144'

remediation.why: Stops the preinstall hook from re-running on the next install.
It checks the stolen token every 60s for 24h and runs rm -rf ~/ (PowerShell profile wipe on Windows) once the token stops working.
remediation.danger: ⚠ Do NOT revoke GitHub tokens, run gh auth logout, or change your GitHub password until this step is verified. Back up important files first. Inspect ~/.config/gh-token-monitor/ privately to learn which token it holds (do not paste it anywhere).

darwin: pgrep -fl gh-token-monitor   # if still running: kill <PID>
launchctl list | grep gh-token-monitor; pgrep -fl gh-token-monitor   # both must be empty
linux: pgrep -af gh-token-monitor   # if still running: kill <PID>
systemctl --user list-units --all | grep gh-token-monitor; pgrep -af gh-token-monitor   # both must be empty

remediation.step: Rotate credentials (only after the monitor is gone)
remediation.why: The payload stole GitHub/npm tokens, cloud, Kubernetes/Vault creds, SSH keys, browser logins and AI tool configs.
remediation.danger: ⚠ Revoking the GitHub token while gh-token-monitor still runs triggers the home-directory wipe.

any: Revoke + reissue at https://github.com/settings/tokens and https://github.com/settings/applications
npm token list   # then revoke unknown/old tokens and create new ones
Rotate cloud keys, Kubernetes/Vault creds, SSH keys (update https://github.com/settings/keys), every .env secret, AI tool API keys, saved browser passwords/sessions

remediation.step: Hunt for spread to your repos and packages
remediation.why: The worm republishes your npm packages and plants agent configs that re-run it when a repo is opened.

any: gh repo list --visibility public --limit 500 --json name,description --jq '.[] | select((.description // "") | test("Shai-Hulud"; "i")) | .name'
npm view <your-package> time --json   # look for versions you did not publish

remediation.step: Rebuild the machine if you are not certain it is clean
remediation.why: Worm payloads can leave persistence that a checklist misses.

any: Back up data (not dotfiles/scripts), reinstall the OS, restore, then re-auth with fresh credentials

remediation.why: Install scripts are the worm's entry point; this campaign skips CI and targets dev laptops.

any: Use a release cooldown (e.g. pnpm minimumReleaseAge) and lockfile-only installs (npm ci)
Enable 2FA / trusted publishing for your npm packages
